We must keep distribution records for color additive batches covered by certificates. The records must show: (1) each quantity used from the batch, including the date and kind of use; and (2) the date and quantity of each shipment or delivery, along with the name and post-office address of the recipient. These records must be kept separately from all other records. They must be made available to FDA or any officer acting on behalf of the Secretary of Health and Human Services at all reasonable hours until at least 2 years after the disposal of all such color additive [1].  

21 CFR 80.39(b)(1) requires that each quantity used from a batch be recorded, along with the date and kind of such use [3].  
21 CFR 80.39(b)(2) requires that the date and quantity of each shipment or delivery be recorded, including the name and post-office address of the person to whom it was delivered [4].  
21 CFR 80.39(a) requires that records be made available until at least 2 years after disposal of all such color additive [1].  
21 CFR 80.39(c) requires that the records required by paragraph (a) be kept separately from all other records [5].
